solution: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives BOTH roots \(\dfrac{17 \pm \sqrt{33}}{2}\). Squaring \(\sqrt{x} = 8 - x\) introduces an extraneous root: the equation requires \(8 - x \ge 0\), and at \(x = \dfrac{17 + \sqrt{33}}{2} \approx 11.372\) the left side is \(+0.372\) while the right is \(-6.372\). Only \(x = \dfrac{17 - \sqrt{33}}{2} \approx 5.628\) satisfies the original equation, where both sides equal \(-0.628\).]

solution: [Textbook misprint: the item is printed \(\log_{1/2}(-8) = 3\), which is false twice over — the argument is negative, and \(\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}\). The book's key answers \(8 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-3}\), i.e. it reads the question as \(\log_{1/2} 8 = -3\): the minus sign was typeset onto the \(8\) instead of the \(3\). The intended question is solved above.]
